rationale: The two Apple idioms a plausible-looking grammar gets wrong, pinned together because each one hid the other. (1) `typedef NS_ENUM(Underlying, Name) { ... };` carries its name INSIDE the macro's arguments and has no trailing declarator — the opposite of every typedef the grammar already handled, so the body collapsed into ERROR nodes and 152 of 164 member constants across 35 declarations were invisible (7.3% recovery, measured over the router's 329-file universe). Taking the FIRST identifier instead of the LAST would name every such enum after its underlying type, so 35 enums would collide on one owner; the members' ownerName is what catches that. (2) A bare macro line above an @interface INSIDE a #if: tree-sitter-c builds a file-scope preproc_if body from _block_item, not _top_level_item, so a rule registered only in _top_level_item is unreachable inside every conditional. sdwebimage wraps most of its headers in `#if SD_UIKIT || SD_MAC`, and the ERROR node the fallthrough produced ran 101 lines to the next @end — deleting a whole class and replacing its properties with phantoms named after the property ATTRIBUTES. The forbidSymbols half is the specific wrongness that has to stay forbidden, because a swallowed class produces a plausible-looking symbol list rather than an obvious failure. Verified to FAIL on the pre-fix wasm: that build emits `type:GuardedModeManual` — a phantom named after an enum MEMBER — and loses GuardedTraits entirely. A FOURTH Apple macro shape — a bracketing `NS_ASSUME_NONNULL_BEGIN` whose successor is a `typedef` rather than an @-declaration — is deliberately ABSENT from this fixture: the only rule measured for it was order-dependent in grammar.js and could not be reproduced or pinned, so it was reverted and the residue is recorded in grammars/tree-sitter-objc/grammar.js rather than pinned as a passing expectation. (3) A trailing availability annotation — a macro CALL with nested parens, commas and a string — is unreachable by C's macro_type_specifier (`MACRO(type)`) and by attribute_specifier (`[[...]]`), and the ERROR it produced swallowed the ENCLOSING @protocol: 83 lines, one protocol, deleted, which is 66 of the lane's 285 remaining errors across the two copies of SDImageCacheDefine.h. The method NAMES are pinned rather than an error count, because a swallowed protocol yields a file with no methods in it and nothing a reader would blame on the protocol. The forbidSymbols half keeps the selector identity clean: an annotation trailing a parameter used to be read as another selector, publishing a method literally named `setDidFinishEventsForBackgroundURLSessionBlock:AF_API_UNAVAILABLE`, and a selector IS identity in Objective-C — that is a method a consumer would route calls to that does not exist.
